problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
s(t)={t}^{2}-2t+\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=3.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

feedback.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{t}^{2}-12t,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-12t) \\  & =6t-12\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1,$ the velocity is

$$
v(1)=6(1)-12=-6.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-6|=6.$
